chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: How much tape the Smithsonian wants
summary: Talk of the five hours of tape needed and who transcribes it.

story.theme_name: Tape changes, reel headers and session breaks
story.community_name: Tape changes, reel headers and session breaks

blocks.x: That's true. What else have you got to talk about, Charles?
I haven't got anything to talk about, man. That's your job. You got a hard job.
You're going to have three hours of tapes, or what?
No. All together, they want five hours of tape, I think. I think that's what they want.
They're going to take the tapes or you got to write it out?
No, thank God, thank God, I don't have to do that. That's one of the hardest things. No, you just send them the tapes.
Yeah, they want -- they have somebody to transcribe it, but they basically want to hear you talking in your own lovely, sweet, dulcet tones, there.
A strange time. I'm doing the best I can do, man.
You're doing very well. Let me turn it off for a minute.
